evals.prompt: I'm building a side project in Next.js where users sign up and save personal documents. Audience is technical, maybe 1k users in year one. Help me think through how to handle authentication for this side project - I haven't picked an approach yet.
evals.expected_output: Skill activates: the prompt supplies enough context (framework, scale, audience) to clear the 'sufficient context' gate. Variance sketch produces three distinct L1 questions (managed provider feature focus vs framework built-in OAuth mix vs roll-your-own session model). Widget renders with 3 L0 branches each leading to a different next-question.

evals.prompt: I'm a TypeScript developer with weekend hours free and want to build a small SaaS I'd actually use myself. I've shipped a couple of side projects before so I'm comfortable picking my own stack. Help me figure out what to build.
evals.expected_output: Skill activates: bounded ideation with distinct L0 problem-spaces (personal admin vs information overload vs work productivity), each leading to a different L1 friction question.

evals.prompt: We have an internal content system where every editorial document also has a 'pair' - a translated or localised counterpart. We're adding support for multiple variant drafts (A/B copy, regional spelling tweaks) per document pair, and need to settle on a data model before we touch the schema. How should we model variants in the document pair store?
evals.expected_output: Skill activates: architecture decision with three distinct L1 questions (migration strategy vs shim location vs routing criteria) under three meaningfully different L0 approaches.

evals.prompt: It's my partner's birthday at the end of October and I want to surprise them with a weekend trip from London. Budget around £400 each total. They like food, walking, and quieter places over big cities. Help me plan where to go.
evals.expected_output: Skill activates: trip planning with distinct destination categories (coastal vs country vs European city break) leading to different L1 questions per category.

evals.prompt: Pick a database for me. We're building a read-heavy product analytics service with ad-hoc queries over the last 90 days of events. Team is 3 backend devs with mostly Postgres experience. We're moving off SQLite because the scale is outgrowing it.
evals.expected_output: Skill activates without keyword overlap to the description's example phrasings. Variance produces meaningfully different L1 questions per L0 (e.g. column-store vs document vs relational each leading to different operational concerns).

evals.prompt: What's the best way to structure folders for a monorepo containing a Next.js web app, a React Native mobile app, and a shared package layer? Team is 5 devs and we want new joiners to find things fast.
evals.expected_output: Skill activates on a 'what's the best way to' phrasing not present in the description. Variance produces different L1 questions across L0 (e.g. feature-based vs layer-based vs platform-based folder strategies).

evals.prompt: I just got a £15k bonus and want to use it deliberately rather than letting it disappear. Mid-thirties, no debt, comfortable salary, already have 6 months emergency fund. Considering some mix of investing, home upgrades, and a course or two. Help me figure out how to allocate it.
evals.expected_output: Skill activates in a domain (personal finance) not present in the description's example list. Variance produces distinct L1 questions across L0 (e.g. tax-advantaged investing vs property vs skill-building each leading to different next-decisions).

evals.prompt: Our Node API is hitting CPU limits at 8k RPS and the roadmap has us 4x'ing traffic over the next 6 months. Team is 4 backend devs, mostly comfortable in Node, some Go familiarity. What's the right move to handle the next traffic tier?
evals.expected_output: Skill activates on a 'what's the right move' phrasing. Variance produces different L1 questions across L0 (e.g. scale-up vs scale-out vs language-rewrite each opening different sub-decisions).
